newsitem.title: USA: Democrats gain in U.S. governors' races.
newsitem.headline: Democrats gain in U.S. governors' races.

text.p: President Clinton's coattails swept a number of Democrats into governors' offices on Tuesday including into at least one traditionally Republican stronghold -- New Hampshire.
New Hampshire voters elected State Sen. Jeanne Shaheen the first woman governor in the state's history and the first Democrat in the post since 1980, according to television projections.

Shaheen defeated Republican Ovide Lamontagne 64 percent to 33 percent in New England's most conservative state. She even won in Lamontagne's own ward in state capitol Manchester. Incumbent Republican Stephen Merrill chose not to seek re-election.

"What we're seeing is in large measure the effect of Clinton's coattails," said University of New Hampshire political science professor Clark Huddard. "After all, the president was here campaigning for Shaheen and the other Democrats."

Indiana, which has a history of voting Republican, elected Democratic candidate Frank O'Bannon governor, according to television projections. O'Bannon, the state's lieutenant governor, defeated Indianapolis' Republican mayor Stephen Goldsmith in what had been a close race to succeed retiring Democrat Evan Bayh.

But in West Virginia, a traditionally Democratic stronghold, former Republican Gov. Cecil Underwood was leading the Democratic nominee and former coal miner's daughter Charlotte Pritt 50 percent to 47 percent, with 65 percent of the precincts reporting.
Some 11 of the 50 states were holding elections for governor, with Democrats defending seven of those seats and Republicans four.
In Washington state, Democrat Gary Locke appeared likely to become the first Asian-American governor on the nation's mainland as he went up against Republican former state Sen. Ellen Craswell.

Democrats prevailed in North Carolina, where incumbent Jim Hunt defeated Republican challenger Robin Hayes and in Vermont where incumbent Howard Dean beat Republican John Gropper. Delaware incumbent Thomas Carper beat Republican Janet Rzwenicki and in Missouri Mel Carnahan defeated Republican Margaret Kelley.

Republicans kept the governor mansion in Utah, where incumbent Mike Leavitt defeated Democrat Jim Bradley. North Dakota incumbent Edward Schafer beat back Democrat State Representative Lee Kaldor. And in Montana, incumbent Marc Racicot defeated Democrat Judy Jacobsen.
Jacobson had been the candidate for lieutentant governor, but her name was placed at the top after her running mate Chet Blaylock, 71, died from a heart attack only two weeks before the election.
